roles.title: Owner
roles.description: Pays for the project, sets standards, and approves major decisions.
responsibilities: Define project goals, budget, and success criteria
Approve major changes and scope adjustments
Enforce quality and performance standards
roles.context: Meta is the Owner on the El Paso data center project. Every decision on site ultimately traces back to meeting Meta's requirements.

roles.title: Architect / Engineer of Record
roles.description: Designs the building and certifies that construction matches the approved design.
responsibilities: Produce drawings and specifications
Answer RFIs (Requests for Information)
Review and approve or reject submittals
roles.context: On a hyperscale project like Meta El Paso, the design team is large and specialized — structural, MEP, civil, and low-voltage engineers all issue their own drawing sets.

roles.title: General Contractor (GC)
roles.description: Manages the overall construction effort, hires subcontractors, and is contractually responsible for delivering the project.
responsibilities: Contract and coordinate all subcontractors
Own the master schedule and budget
Report progress and risk to the Owner
roles.context: JE Dunn Construction is the GC (co-GC with Hensel Phelps) on Meta El Paso. This is the company you're interviewing with.

roles.title: Superintendent
roles.description: The senior field leader responsible for day-to-day site operations, safety, and schedule.
responsibilities: Run the daily/weekly schedule and trade sequencing
Own site safety and enforce site rules
Direct Field Engineers and resolve escalations
roles.context: The Superintendent is your direct field leader — the person you escalate to and the person whose trust you're building every day.

roles.title: Field Engineer (FE)
roles.description: The eyes, ears, and documentation engine of the field team — verifying that what's being built matches the drawings and specs.
responsibilities: Perform layout and quality inspections
Track RFIs, submittals, and punch list items
Document daily progress and coordinate between trades and the office
roles.context: This is you. You sit between the office (PM, Super) and the field trades — translating design intent into verified, documented reality.

roles.title: Trade Foreman
roles.description: Leads a specific crew (concrete, electrical, mechanical, etc.) and directs their daily work.
responsibilities: Assign daily tasks to the crew
Coordinate material and equipment needs
Communicate progress and issues to the FE/Super
roles.context: You will work with dozens of foremen across trades. Building trust with them is as important as your relationship with the Super.

roles.title: Craft Workers
roles.description: The tradespeople physically installing the work — carpenters, electricians, pipefitters, laborers, etc.
responsibilities: Install work per drawings and specifications
Follow safety protocols
Flag issues to their foreman
roles.context: Thousands of craft workers will be on site at peak for Meta El Paso. You won't direct them personally — that's the foreman's job — but your inspections affect their work daily.

reportingNote: You sit here: between the office PM/Super chain and the field trades. Information flows up to you (from foremen) and down to you (from the Super), and you're responsible for making sure both sides have accurate, timely information.
